The FY2026 10-K, due roughly late October 2026, is where the full-year LIFO reserve roll-forward and any IEEPA tariff refund or gain-contingency disclosure will appear in primary form; CBP's CAPE liquidation process was still running at ~$128.7bn of accepted refunds as of 2026-07-31, so supplier pass-back to AZO continues to accrue after this print.

Nike's FY27 guide assumed incremental tariffs of 10% through July then 15% thereafter, but when Section 122 expired on 2026-07-24 it was replaced by a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% depending on the country (Vietnam at 12.5%), so the rate on goods landing from August is 2.5-5 points below plan, a gross-margin tailwind that can only show up in the Q2/H2 margin guide.

China retail kept falling through the quarter: Pou Sheng (Yue Yuen's China retail arm, a Nike and Adidas reseller) posted August revenue -9% y/y and Topsports' March-May sales fell by a low-teens percentage, while Nike's own termination of online authorisations for thousands of China resellers from 2027-01-01 adds a headwind to the H2 China guide.

Street Q2 EPS of $0.53 already sits on the ceiling of Nike's own 'flattish earnings ex-tariff-recovery' framework for Q4 FY26-Q2 FY27 (prior-year $0.14 + $0.49 + $0.53 = $1.16; Q4 FY26 ex-benefit delivered $0.20, so Q1+Q2 needs ~$0.96 against consensus $0.44 + $0.53 = $0.97), while Nike pre-flagged a multipoint sequential revenue deceleration into Q2 and UBS expects an implied Q2 of $0.31-0.43.

The bar has been cut hard into the print — Baird to Neutral (PT $70 to $44), BofA to Underperform ($30), Morgan Stanley Underweight ($31), BMO Underperform ($30), Piper, Citi, UBS, Telsey and Evercore ($34) target cuts, S&P 100 removal on 2026-09-21 — with record short interest of ~87M shares, while Jefferies (2026-09-28) expects a Q1 beat at $11.5bn / $0.48.
